business-domain-context

Business domain map

What Bunkai TMS is, how it earns, and what each domain term means.

Overview

Bunkai is an open-core Test Management System (multi-tenant SaaS plus self-host). It is a TMS whose data model enforces structure: an ATC cannot exist without a user story, a test chains ATCs, a bug carries its module and optional run/ATC. Actors are workspace members (viewer, member, admin, owner) plus AI agents and CI acting through personal access tokens.

As of 2026-10-05 the live staging schema has 35 public tables (legacy glossary of 2026-05-23 listed 11): the original tenancy and ATC core plus tests, runs, bugs, test plans, milestones, environments, notifications, billing and workspace export/deletion.

Business model

Problem. Incumbent TMSs (Xray, Zephyr, TestRail) are document vaults: test cases without structure, no link to story or criterion, broken traceability, bug management delegated to Jira. Regulated industries also cannot store specs on third-party SaaS.

Solution. Enforce structure in the data model so good QA is the path of least resistance; API-first so AI agents and CI operate it; open-core so teams can self-host.

TierIncludesPricing (from business-model, unverified in code)
Communityself-hosted core: ATCs, tests, runs, bugs, REST API, CLIfree, OSS
Cloudsame code, hostedper-seat subscription (target not final)
EnterpriseSSO/SAML, audit log, enterprise integrations, SLAannual license

The tier maps to workspaces.plan (community, cloud, enterprise); checkout is tracked in billing_checkout_sessions and Stripe webhooks in stripe_webhook_events. Segments: indie QA teams, mid-market engineering orgs on Jira+Xray, regulated enterprises, and the UPEX Galaxy training audience (adoption pipeline).

Workspace

Tenant root and billing unit, owned by one user, with a globally unique slug. Membership carries a role and a status; invites can grant viewer, member or admin only (never owner). Deletion and data export are asynchronous jobs (workspace_deletions, workspace_exports). UI label: "Workspace".

Project

The application under test, scoped to a workspace (slug unique per workspace). Owns its modules, stories, ATCs, plans and milestones, and its named environments (project_environments, used when starting a run). UI label: "Project".

Module

Node of the project test-module tree, depth at most 6 with a materialized slash path. Bugs and stories are filed against a module; a bug without a module cannot exist. UI label: "Module".

User Story

Business intent unit anchored to a module, linkable to Jira via external_id / external_url (e.g. BK-123). Status is draft or ready_to_test. Traceability reports per story exist (migrations 0068-0069). UI label: "User Story".

Acceptance Criterion (AC)

Ordered criterion of a user story, unique by position. It is the anchor an ATC must verify. UI label: "Acceptance Criterion" / "AC".

ATC (Acceptance Test Case)

The reusable, versioned unit of testing. Layer is UI, API or Unit; priority and technique (EP, BVA, State Transition, Decision Table, Pairwise) are optional classification fields added in migration 0087. Anchored NOT NULL to a user story (ON DELETE RESTRICT) and to at least one AC through the M:N table. Saving through the save RPC bumps version so every test chaining it sees the edit. Product copy uses "ATC", "Acceptance Test Case" and "Acceptance Test Case" as synonyms. Steps and assertions are ordered children.

Test

An ordered chain of ATCs (title, tags, version) at workspace level. A run executes a test and snapshots its title (runs.test_title). Reintroduced as a table since the legacy glossary, which said no tests table existed.

Run

One execution of a test against a project environment by an executor: human, agent or ci. Status moves running to passed, failed or aborted (abort carries a reason; an inactivity sweep also aborts, migration 0075). Per-ATC and per-step results live in run_atcs / run_steps. A start token makes starts idempotent.

Bug

Native defect anchored to workspace, project and module, optionally to the run, run step and ATC that exposed it. Severity P1-P4, status open, in_progress, resolved, closed, optional assignee and evidence URLs. Jira sync is optional, not a delegation.

Test Plan

Named plan with a goal, grouping tests through test_plan_tests. Status open or closed. Added in migrations 0073-0076.

Milestone

Project-level target-date marker with name and description (migration 0064).

Personal Access Token (PAT)

Bearer credential for CLI and AI agents, format bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>, soft-revoked, scoped to atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin. A PAT cannot mint another PAT. Magic-link tokens belong to passwordless sign-in. UI label: "Personal Access Token" / "PAT" / "API Token".

Notification

In-app and email notifications for run lifecycle, bug lifecycle and mentions, with per-user channel preferences and a digest log (pending, sent, failed).

Feature flag

Boolean flag keyed per scope: global or workspace, with a JSON payload.

QA inspector roles

Database roles (read-only and read-write) provisioned for QA inspection of the database; not an application role (migrations 0085-0088). Relevant to how this repo reads staging through DBHub.

Discovery gaps

  • Pricing numbers and the OSS license (Apache vs MIT) come from business-model and are not verifiable in code.
  • Meaning of import_jobs and idempotency_keys inferred from table names and statuses; business flow not traced.
  • No UI-copy pass was done over app/ and components/: UI-label mapping carried from the legacy glossary (English only) plus names seen in schema.
  • Status values of project_environments and milestones (no CHECK) not enumerated; environment names are free text.
  • Persona names (Elena, Mateo, Sara, Karim) are in the legacy PRD; not re-verified.
  • Whether the PAT scope list is exhaustive: only four literals found in code, no CHECK in DB.
  • Legacy glossary state machines (atcs.status, membership) not re-verified against current triggers; belongs to business-data-context.
